newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The documentary "Deng Xiaoping" broadcast on China's CCTV last week received strong reaction from audiences throughout the country.
-- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said Hong Kong's young people should develop a sense of belonging and responsibility towards the territory.
-- MING PAO -- Reliable sources said the health of Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping was stable, the evidence being that most of his family were on holiday in Hainan province.
-- Research showed that 35 percent of mainland job seekers expect to be paid at 2,000 yuan a month, while six percent hoped their monthly salaries would exceed 10,000 yuan.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Zhou Nan, the director of the Hong Kong branch of China's Xinhua news agency said he was expecting to retire after the handover on July 1.
-- DAILY NEWS -- Hospital staff threatened to take industrial action to protest against the decision of the Hospital Authority to hire new staff on contract rather than giving them permanent jobs.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- HongKong Telecom and Hutchison Whampoa failed to get a slice of eight Taiwan mobile phone franchises on Monday.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China Eastern Airlines, the mainland's first airline to list abroad, warned that profitability would be hampered by heavy reliance on external financing to fund future expansion.
-- China's move to use foreign exchange reserves to purchase power generating equipment underscored its intention to develop its power sector quickly.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Seven top U.S. pension fund managers with combined assets of more than US$234 billion visited Hong Kong on Monday to seek new investment opportunities.
